newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Gold-Robust output despite price.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Gold-Robust output despite price.

text.p: Australian mining companies are returning robust December quarter production figures, undeterred by a soft gold price at home and internationally.

Acacia Resources Ltd this week said December quarter production was up 54 percent saw big increases in gold yields. Resolute Samantha Ltd saw output rise 19 percent in the three months to December 31 to 88,851 ounces and is aiming to further boost its reserves through exploration.

"The company is budgeting to spend A$30 milion on exploration activities in 1997 under a major programme, which currently has about 32 rigs operating on various sites," Resolute's managing director, Michael Carrick said.

Great Central Mines NL, part of the stable of mines controlled by Joseph Gutnick, maintains it will reach its forecasted production of 550,000 ounces in 1996/97 despite problems occurring at its Jundee and Bronzewing deposits in Western Australia in the last quarter.
Meanwhile junior miner Consolidated Gold NL believes it will become a 100,000-ounce plus producer this year as its Davyhurst gold project comes on stream in June

Most Australian gold production is hedged forward at prices well above the current market, so there is little impetus to curtail output. Perth-based miner Ross Mining NL which produced about 19,456 ounces of gold in the last quarter holds hedge positions for 54,156 ounces for a weighted average price of A$561 an ounce -- over A$100 an ounce above the current spot market. Consolidated Gold has hedges on 200,000 ounces.
Despite the hedge positions, producers still found it profitable to sell into the latest price rally, although on a local level were not the dominant players, dealers said.
After hitting three year lows in mid-January of around US$347 an ounce, gold bounced showed signs of a recovery.
"This had a lot to do with proft-takers selling into the market, not just producers," one dealer said.
Spot bullion currently fetches about US$351.00-$351.50 an ounce. In Australain dollars the price is about A$455.00-$455.50 an ounce.
Dealers said US$350 remains a critical technical point, although good buying at current levels has allayed some concerns the price will be tested soon.
However, the perception that there is plenty of gold to go around is doing little to polish the precious metals image among local investors.
"Sometimes a commodity, sometimes not, gold's a funny one," said one dealer.

The latest Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) forecast, due out next week, is expected to show local producers are on track to produce a record of around 300 tonnes of gold in 1996/97 (July-June), up from about 262 tonnes in 1996/96.
